title: High Temperature Fan Construction
description: FanPedia's general construction drawing for high temperature centrifugal fans (p. 110), with its three drive-end close-ups, carrying seven numbered markers, leader lines and a label column. Explore mode previews each part's name and description; quiz mode hides the labels and describes each part by its job, with two attempts, a hint after the first miss and mastery at 6 of 7 on the first attempt.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: High temperature construction features of a centrifugal fan
learningObjectives: The learner will identify the seven labeled high temperature construction features of a centrifugal fan (shaft seal, bearing, shaft cooler, insulation pins, raised access door, safety screen and cooler box) on FanPedia's drawing, given each feature's job.

accessibility.notes: The drawing is a labelled SVG group; every numbered marker is a focusable role=button and Tab walks them in number order; Enter or Space selects one; focus or hover previews its name and description. During the quiz the markers are named only 'Part n' until resolved, labels and leader lines are hidden, and hints never name the answer. Verdicts and prompts are announced through FP.announce (aria-live). ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and an 'Answer' badge pair with colour. Text is 12 px or larger; markers keep a constant pixel size; the label column moves below the drawing on narrow screens.

simulation.modelType: labeled diagram with locate quiz (FP.Overlay callout engine on FP.CalloutQuiz)
rules: Explore mode: hover or focus previews a part's name and description; click, Enter or Space opens it and counts it as visited; never scored.
Quiz mode: 7 prompts in a seeded shuffle (the same order for every learner; Start over reshuffles).
Two attempts per prompt; the first wrong answer shows a hint that does not name the answer; the second reveals the answer and counts as missed.
Selecting empty space uses no attempt.
Only first-attempt answers count toward mastery; mastery is 6 of 7.
assumptions: FanPedia p. 110 high temperature general construction drawing and its pedestal close-ups, with the printed labels removed; marker positions are percentages of the image.
limitations: The drawing is FanPedia's, not a specific current catalog model; the colour legend, captions and cooler box note of the original page are not shown, and the middle close-up (shaft cooler with a stuffing box or mechanical seal) has no marker.

sources: FanPedia p. 110 (Special Construction: High Temperature, Centrifugal Fans, General Construction, Arrangements 1, 8, 9, 9F, 10, with the high temp style pedestal insets): drawing and part names
FanPedia p. 90 (high temperature style pedestal), p. 117 (raised access door), p. 192 (shaft cooler): descriptions
Drawing: FanPedia, Twin City Fan, p. 110

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore labelled markers on the real FanPedia drawing first, then retrieval practice: find each part from a description of its job, with a hint after the first miss and immediate correction.
keyQuestions: Which part sheds the heat that travels along the shaft, and what is it protecting?
Why is the area around the shaft cooler left uninsulated on an insulated housing?
commonMisconceptions: A cooler box is an insulated enclosure.
The shaft cooler cools the airstream.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 7'; mastery is 6 of 7 on the first attempt.
